headline: Toyota commits to gigacasting; European aluminium scrap supply tightens

summary.text: Toyota plans gigacasting for Lexus and possibly bZ4X EVs in China, showing another OEM moving body structures toward single-piece castings, which could reduce demand for multi-part structural castings.
European scrap exports are deepening the regional aluminium shortage, which could raise input costs for the recycled-content alloys Lindner relies on.
Germany remains an anchor of Europe's recycled aluminium production, and treating scrap as a standard raw material could help secure low-CO2 feedstock.
Competitor Nemak reported revenue and EBITDA growth of over 21% while impairments left results near break-even, so it is expanding but under some pressure.
An arXiv review of autonomous AI inspection (NDE 4.0) is academic, but it may inform the X-ray defect-detection roadmap.

actions.text: Sales lead: ask key OEM and Tier-1 contacts about gigacasting plans and pitch mid-size integrated castings or tooling know-how as a complement.
Purchasing: check scrap and recycled-aluminium supply contracts for 2027 and quantify exposure to the European scrap shortage.
Quality manager: review the NDE 4.0 paper for ideas applicable to X-ray inspection and report back.

items.title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection
items.snippet: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current NDI landscape, analyzing the field through four distinct lenses, namely, computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives. We synthesize a broad range of academic literature to illustrate the rapid evolution from manual, analog interpretation to a digitized, data-centric paradigm known as NDE…
items.reason: Review of autonomous AI-driven inspection algorithms informs Lindner's X-ray inspection and defect detection roadmap, though it is academic rather than industrial.
